title.narrative: Improvement of municipal solid waste management through digitisation, innovation and pilot projects in selected intermediate and small cities within the framework of a just transition.

description.narrative: The project aims to improve solid waste management at the national level in Bolivia through the implementation of planning components, the development of digital tools, and the development of pilot projects. All this will be done in careful alignment with the Political Constitution of the State, the Patriotic Agenda of the Bicentennial 2025, and the guidelines of the Economic and Social Development Plan 2021-2025. It also seeks to integrate the Sectoral Plans for Integral Development 2021-2025 of both the Ministry of Environment and Water (MMAyA) and the Ministry of Public Works, Services and Housing (MOPSV). Therefore, it is proposed that the project consider the following cross-cutting aspects: • Capacity building for waste management: The objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of national and local stakeholders in integrated waste management, with a special focus on adaptation to climate change. It seeks to provide tools and knowledge to effectively address the challenges associated with this process, with an emphasis on the implementation of sustainable practices. • Development of Information Systems (Integrated Waste Management Information System - SIGIR): The objective is to support the development and implementation of a data collection and visualization tool for integrated waste management at the national level. This tool will enable relevant institutions to monitor waste management at the municipal level. The main objective is to develop a modular and interoperable information system that allows data collection, storage, and visualization, including report generation and process simplification for agile and timely decision-making. The tool to be developed will use existing platforms and will be implemented through open-source software with open standards, based on the available technical capacities, integrating and linking the current calculation and analysis tools of the MMAyA.This platform is being implemented as a mechanism to strengthen the institutional capacity of the Ministry, considering that it will promote compliance with Law 755 - Integrated Waste Management Law. Article 20 of this law establishes the need to implement an information system to manage national and territorial information for this specific sector, whose design and management will be the responsibility of the MMAyA. The activities of the project will help to ensure that the system meets the requirements of this law, which states that "the system must contain permanent and updated information on the waste generated and valorized, the infrastructure, and technologies used for its management, information on authorized operators and other aspects...". • Development of innovative models: The project proposes developing at least five innovative models based on the systematization of previous local experience in solid waste management. These models will be designed to provide viable technical alternatives for the closure of landfills, their controlled management, waste reduction, and the implementation of appropriate final disposal solutions. Furthermore, their formulation will be based on the criteria and typologies agreed with the MMyA, including technical, financial, legal, social, and environmental components. Since inclusiveness is a fundamental aspect of the initiative, the models will include schemes for the participation of waste collectors and recyclers, with special emphasis to women. • Inclusion as an axis of integrated waste management: The project will support waste collectors and informal recyclers through the following activities: First, a characterization will be carried out to understand their general conditions and characteristics. Second, guidelines will be developed for their formal integration into the solid waste management process. This process will incorporate a gender transformative approach perspective by analyzing the number of women currently present in the sector, their status (formal/informal; low level / managerial positions), their working conditions, and any specific exclusions they might be facing by taking an intersectional approach in the population characterization human rights and gender analysis, to design strategies and action plans adapted to their specific needs and experiences, both in the immediate and in the long term. • Implementation of pilot projects and plans: The project aims to implement a plan and a pilot project in cities with less than 15,000 inhabitants. The plan aims to support a local government in the development of its integrated waste management program, addressing technical, financial, regulatory, and social aspects.
